title: "Notes and open questions"

---

## Limitations

Three deliberately chosen seeds cannot tell us what a typical initial
condition will do. They illustrate distinct behaviors, but say little
about the frequency of those behaviors or the variety of more complex
patterns.

The grid is unbounded and the update is synchronous. Finite boundaries,
noise, or a different update order would define a different experiment.

## What I would try next

- Sample random initial conditions at several densities and track how
  long their transients last.
- Detect repeating patterns up to translation, so moving patterns do not
  appear unrelated at every step.
- Compare population with spatial measurements, such as occupied area
  and the number of connected components.

## A useful project record

Even a tiny experiment benefits from a precise seed, a stated update rule,
reproducible code, and an explanation of what the measurements leave out.
The same structure can hold a much larger project: an overview for the main
idea, an experiment page for the evidence, and notes for unfinished work.
